parsedVerdict.reasoning: The use case does the right application work: it loads the order through the domain repository port, delegates the state change to the domain (order.transitionTo), saves the order, and raises a not-found error. But `execute` also takes untyped `any` inputs and unpacks them the way an HTTP framework delivers request values. It checks whether the order ID or new state is an array and takes the first element. Otherwise it accepts only a string, falls back to an empty string, and casts the result to OrderStateType without checking it. This handles transport-specific input shapes, typical of Express params or query values (`string | string[]`). That job belongs in the infrastructure/presentation adapter (OrderController, which injects this use case), not in the application layer. The use case should accept a typed command (orderId: string, newState: OrderStateType). The transport-parsing responsibility has leaked into the application file, so the unit fails.
